claim: A cell-free LC3 lipidation reaction was previously established to identify the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) as a membrane source for LC3 lipidation.
source: Previously, we established a cell-free LC3 lipidation reaction to identify the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) as a membrane source for LC3 lipidation, a key step of autophagosome biogenesis (Ge et al., eLife 2013; 2:e00947).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Ge et al., eLife 2013; 2:e00947).

claim: LC3 lipidation is a key step of autophagosome biogenesis.
source: Previously, we established a cell-free LC3 lipidation reaction to identify the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) as a membrane source for LC3 lipidation, a key step of autophagosome biogenesis (Ge et al., eLife 2013; 2:e00947).
evidence: The claim is supported by established scientific knowledge and citation.

claim: Starvation activation of autophagic phosphotidylinositol-3 kinase (PI3K) induces the generation of small vesicles active in LC3 lipidation.
source: We now report that starvation activation of autophagic phosphotidylinositol-3 kinase (PI3K) induces the generation of small vesicles active in LC3 lipidation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Subcellular fractionation studies identified the ERGIC as the donor membrane in the generation of small lipidation-active vesicles.
source: Subcellular fractionation studies identified the ERGIC as the donor membrane in the generation of small lipidation-active vesicles.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from subcellular fractionation shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: COPII proteins are recruited to the ERGIC membrane in starved cells, dependent on active PI3K.
source: COPII proteins are recruited to the ERGIC membrane in starved cells, dependent on active PI3K.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Starvation activates the autophagic PI3K, which in turn induces the recruitment of COPII to the ERGIC to bud LC3 lipidation-active vesicles as one potential membrane source of the autophagosome.
source: We conclude that starvation activates the autophagic PI3K, which in turn induces the recruitment of COPII to the ERGIC to bud LC3 lipidation-active vesicles as one potential membrane source of the autophagosome.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Macroautophagy is a conserved cellular process wherein cytoplasmic protein and organelles are packaged and delivered to the lysosome to promote survival under conditions of stress.
source: Macroautophagy (hereafter autophagy) is a conserved cellular process wherein cytoplasmic protein and organelles are packaged and delivered to the lysosome to promote survival under conditions of stress (Choi et al., 2013; Jiang and Mizushima, 2014; Mizushima et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The autophagy process begins with the formation of a double-membrane organelle, termed the autophagosome.
source: The process begins with the formation of a double-membrane organelle, termed the autophagosome, which envelops part of the cytoplasm for targeting to and degradation in the lysosome (Burman and Ktistakis, 2010; Weidberg et al., 2011; Hamasaki et al., 2013b; Lamb et al., 2013; Ge et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The autophagosome envelops part of the cytoplasm for targeting to and degradation in the lysosome.
source: The process begins with the formation of a double-membrane organelle, termed the autophagosome, which envelops part of the cytoplasm for targeting to and degradation in the lysosome (Burman and Ktistakis, 2010; Weidberg et al., 2011; Hamasaki et al., 2013b; Lamb et al., 2013; Ge et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Completion of the autophagosome requires step-wise acquisition of membranes from intracellular organelles directed by proteins devoted to autophagy.
source: Completion of the autophagosome requires step-wise acquisition of membranes from intracellular organelles directed by proteins devoted to autophagy (Mizushima et al., 2011; Rubinsztein et al., 2012; Abada and Elazar, 2014; Feng et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The autophagic phosphotidylinositol-3 kinase (PI3K) complex mediates production of phosphotidylinositol-3 phosphate (PI3P).
source: A direct link between the autophagic signal and the biogenesis of the phagophore membrane is the autophagic phosphotidylinositol-3 kinase (PI3K) complex (VPS34, VPS15, Beclin-1 and ATG14)-mediated production of phosphotidylinositol-3 phosphate (PI3P), an event triggered by starvation (Sun et al., 2008; Matsunaga et al., 2010; Obara and Ohsumi, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The autophagic PI3K complex consists of VPS34, VPS15, Beclin-1 and ATG14.
source: A direct link between the autophagic signal and the biogenesis of the phagophore membrane is the autophagic phosphotidylinositol-3 kinase (PI3K) complex (VPS34, VPS15, Beclin-1 and ATG14)-mediated production of phosphotidylinositol-3 phosphate (PI3P), an event triggered by starvation (Sun et al., 2008; Matsunaga et al., 2010; Obara and Ohsumi, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: PI3P production by the autophagic PI3K complex is triggered by starvation.
source: A direct link between the autophagic signal and the biogenesis of the phagophore membrane is the autophagic phosphotidylinositol-3 kinase (PI3K) complex (VPS34, VPS15, Beclin-1 and ATG14)-mediated production of phosphotidylinositol-3 phosphate (PI3P), an event triggered by starvation (Sun et al., 2008; Matsunaga et al., 2010; Obara and Ohsumi, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: In Atg5 knockout (KO) mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF), autophagosome formation is blocked downstream of the PI3K pathway.
source: In Atg5 knockout (KO) mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF), which are deficient in the terminal step of the LC3 lipidation cascade, autophagosome formation is blocked downstream of the PI3K pathway (Mizushima et al., 2001; Suzuki et al., 2007; Itakura and Mizushima, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Atg5 KO MEFs are deficient in the terminal step of the LC3 lipidation cascade.
source: In Atg5 knockout (KO) mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF), which are deficient in the terminal step of the LC3 lipidation cascade, autophagosome formation is blocked downstream of the PI3K pathway (Mizushima et al., 2001; Suzuki et al., 2007; Itakura and Mizushima, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Membrane precursors acting between the PI3K pathway and phagophore maturation may accumulate in Atg5 KO MEFs after starvation.
source: Therefore, membrane precursors acting between the PI3K pathway and phagophore maturation may accumulate in Atg5 KO MEFs after starvation.
evidence: The claim is a logical inference based on the properties of Atg5 KO MEFs.

claim: LC3 lipidation on untreated membranes was efficiently blocked by the PI3K inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA).
source: Consistent with the previous study, lipidation of LC3 on the untreated membrane was efficiently blocked by a PI3K inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA, ∼sevenfold decrease of activity with the indicated concentration of 3-MA, Figure 1B) or the PI3P blocker FYVE domain protein (∼ninefold and 18-fold decrease of activity with the indicated concentration of FYVE protein, Figure 1C) (Stenmark and Aasland, 1999; Axe et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: LC3 lipidation on untreated membranes was efficiently blocked by the PI3P blocker FYVE domain protein.
source: Consistent with the previous study, lipidation of LC3 on the untreated membrane was efficiently blocked by a PI3K inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA, ∼sevenfold decrease of activity with the indicated concentration of 3-MA, Figure 1B) or the PI3P blocker FYVE domain protein (∼ninefold and 18-fold decrease of activity with the indicated concentration of FYVE protein, Figure 1C) (Stenmark and Aasland, 1999; Axe et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: LC3 lipidation promoted with membranes from starved cells was less sensitive to 3-MA inhibition than membranes from untreated cells.
source: However, LC3 lipidation promoted with membranes from starved cells was less sensitive to 3-MA or FYVE domain protein inhibition (∼threefold decrease with the indicated concentration of 3-MA, Figure 1B, and ∼twofold and fourfold decrease with indicated concentration of FYVE domain protein, Figure 1C), indicating that a later autophagosomal precursor, bypassing the need of PI3K for LC3 lipidation, was generated in response to starvation in Atg5 KO MEFs.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: LC3 lipidation promoted with membranes from starved cells was less sensitive to FYVE domain protein inhibition than membranes from untreated cells.
source: However, LC3 lipidation promoted with membranes from starved cells was less sensitive to 3-MA or FYVE domain protein inhibition (∼threefold decrease with the indicated concentration of 3-MA, Figure 1B, and ∼twofold and fourfold decrease with indicated concentration of FYVE domain protein, Figure 1C), indicating that a later autophagosomal precursor, bypassing the need of PI3K for LC3 lipidation, was generated in response to starvation in Atg5 KO MEFs.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A later autophagosomal precursor, bypassing the need of PI3K for LC3 lipidation, was generated in response to starvation in Atg5 KO MEFs.
source: However, LC3 lipidation promoted with membranes from starved cells was less sensitive to 3-MA or FYVE domain protein inhibition (∼threefold decrease with the indicated concentration of 3-MA, Figure 1B, and ∼twofold and fourfold decrease with indicated concentration of FYVE domain protein, Figure 1C), indicating that a later autophagosomal precursor, bypassing the need of PI3K for LC3 lipidation, was generated in response to starvation in Atg5 KO MEFs.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the differential sensitivity to PI3K inhibitors.

claim: The 25K membrane from untreated cells had the highest lipidation activity compared to 3K and 100K membrane pellet fractions.
source: Consistent with the previous result (Ge et al., 2013), the 25K membrane from untreated cells had the highest activity whereas neither the 3K nor the 100K membrane pellet fractions had comparable activity (∼1/7 and 1/3 of the activity of the 25K membrane in the 3K and 100K membrane respectively, Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Starvation or PI3K inhibition did not substantially affect the lipidation activity in the 3K or 25K fractions.
source: Starvation or PI3K inhibition did not substantially affect the lipidation activity in the 3K or 25K fractions (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The 100K membrane from starved cells displayed a ∼1.5-fold increase of lipidation activity compared to that of membranes from untreated cells.
source: However, the 100K membrane from starved cells, mainly containing small vesicles, displayed a ∼1.5-fold increase of lipidation activity compared to that of membranes from untreated cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The 100K membrane fraction mainly contains small vesicles.
source: However, the 100K membrane from starved cells, mainly containing small vesicles, displayed a ∼1.5-fold increase of lipidation activity compared to that of membranes from untreated cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of differential centrifugation and membrane fractionation.

claim: Addition of PI3K inhibitors to cells during starvation abolished the increase of lipidation activity in the 100K membrane induced by starvation.
source: Addition of PI3K inhibitors to cells during starvation abolished the increase of lipidation activity in the 100K membrane induced by starvation (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Starvation induces the formation of small membranes competent for LC3 lipidation in a process that requires activation of the PI3K.
source: Therefore, starvation induces the formation of small membranes competent for LC3 lipidation in a process that requires activation of the PI3K.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1E.

claim: Lipidation activity in the 25K membranes was inhibited by PI3K inhibitors 3-MA and wortmannin in a dose dependent manner.
source: Consistent with our previous result, lipidation activity in the 25K membranes was inhibited by PI3K inhibitors 3-MA and wortmannin as well as the PI3P blocker, FYVE domain protein, in a dose dependent manner (Figure 1F,G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F, 1G, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Lipidation activity in the 25K membranes was inhibited by the PI3P blocker FYVE domain protein in a dose dependent manner.
source: Consistent with our previous result, lipidation activity in the 25K membranes was inhibited by PI3K inhibitors 3-MA and wortmannin as well as the PI3P blocker, FYVE domain protein, in a dose dependent manner (Figure 1F,G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F, 1G, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: PI3K inhibitors did not inhibit lipidation activity of the 100K membranes.
source: In contrast, PI3K inhibitors did not inhibit lipidation activity of the 100K membranes (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The FYVE domain protein was less potent in inhibiting LC3 lipidation with membranes in the 100K than the 25K pellet fraction.
source: Likewise, the FYVE domain protein was less potent in inhibiting LC3 lipidation with membranes in the 100K than the 25K pellet fraction (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Membranes in the 100K pellet fraction remained partially sensitive to the FYVE domain protein.
source: Nonetheless, membranes in the 100K pellet fraction remained partially sensitive to the FYVE domain protein suggesting that access of PI3P in these membranes remained critical for the recruitment of factors, such as WIPI2 (Dooley et al., 2014), necessary for the lipidation event.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Access of PI3P in 100K membranes remained critical for the recruitment of factors necessary for the lipidation event.
source: Nonetheless, membranes in the 100K pellet fraction remained partially sensitive to the FYVE domain protein suggesting that access of PI3P in these membranes remained critical for the recruitment of factors, such as WIPI2 (Dooley et al., 2014), necessary for the lipidation event.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the partial sensitivity to FYVE domain protein.

claim: WIPI2 is a factor necessary for the LC3 lipidation event.
source: Nonetheless, membranes in the 100K pellet fraction remained partially sensitive to the FYVE domain protein suggesting that access of PI3P in these membranes remained critical for the recruitment of factors, such as WIPI2 (Dooley et al., 2014), necessary for the lipidation event.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Membranes in the 100K fraction are generated downstream of the PI3K-dependent step.
source: These data suggest that membranes in the 100K fraction are generated downstream of the PI3K-dependent step.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the resistance to PI3K inhibitors.

claim: COPII vesicles were generated in the presence of cytosol, membrane and nucleotide.
source: As shown in Figure 2B, COPII vesicles, marked by the reporter protein SEC22B, were generated in the presence of cytosol, membrane and nucleotide (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: SEC22B is a marker for COPII vesicles.
source: As shown in Figure 2B, COPII vesicles, marked by the reporter protein SEC22B, were generated in the presence of cytosol, membrane and nucleotide (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about COPII vesicle markers.

claim: Starvation signals from the cytosol or inhibition of PI3K activity did not affect the level of budded SEC22B.
source: Starvation signals from the cytosol or inhibition of PI3K activity did not affect the level of budded SEC22B (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Slowly-sedimenting vesicles generated in the cell-free reaction supported LC3 lipidation with a ∼1.5-fold increase in lipidation activity in incubations containing cytosol from starved compared to untreated cells.
source: Slowly-sedimenting vesicles generated in this reaction supported LC3 lipidation with a ∼1.5-fold increase in lipidation activity in incubations containing cytosol from starved compared to untreated cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The stimulatory effect of starved cytosol on LC3 lipidation was compromised by addition of PI3K inhibitors during the small vesicle formation step.
source: This stimulatory effect was compromised by addition of PI3K inhibitors during the small vesicle formation step (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Occlusion of PI3P by FYVE domain protein attenuated the generation of small vesicles active in LC3 lipidation.
source: Occlusion of PI3P by FYVE domain protein also attenuated the generation of small vesicles active in LC3 lipidation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), consistent with the requirement for PI3P production on the donor membrane to generate the vesicles active in the lipidation of LC3.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: PI3P production on the donor membrane is required to generate the vesicles active in the lipidation of LC3.
source: Occlusion of PI3P by FYVE domain protein also attenuated the generation of small vesicles active in LC3 lipidation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), consistent with the requirement for PI3P production on the donor membrane to generate the vesicles active in the lipidation of LC3.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the effect of PI3P occlusion.

claim: Lipidation activity promoted by the small vesicles was resistant to PI3K inhibition but remained partly sensitive to the PI3P blocker peptide.
source: Importantly, lipidation activity promoted by the small vesicles was resistant to PI3K inhibition but remained partly sensitive to the PI3P blocker peptide, which was similar to the behavior of the 100K membrane generated from starved cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The behavior of small vesicles generated in the cell-free reaction was similar to the behavior of the 100K membrane generated from starved cells.
source: Importantly, lipidation activity promoted by the small vesicles was resistant to PI3K inhibition but remained partly sensitive to the PI3P blocker peptide, which was similar to the behavior of the 100K membrane generated from starved cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is an inference from comparing the properties of the two membrane fractions.

claim: A donor membrane generates small vesicles in a starvation-induced and PI3K-dependent manner.
source: The data indicate that a donor membrane generates these small vesicles in a starvation-induced and PI3K-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: SEC22B and ERGIC53 are COPII cargos generated from ER and enriched in ERGIC.
source: The membrane template for COPII budding, marked by SEC22B and ERGIC53 (two COPII cargos generated from ER and enriched in ERGIC; Hauri et al., 2000; Mancias and Goldberg, 2007; Zhang et al., 1999), was enriched in the P fraction, where the majority of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) sedimented (the enrichment of RPN1, an ER marker, Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The membrane template for COPII budding was enriched in the P fraction.
source: The membrane template for COPII budding, marked by SEC22B and ERGIC53 (two COPII cargos generated from ER and enriched in ERGIC; Hauri et al., 2000; Mancias and Goldberg, 2007; Zhang et al., 1999), was enriched in the P fraction, where the majority of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) sedimented (the enrichment of RPN1, an ER marker, Figure 2D).

claim: The majority of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) sedimented in the P fraction.

claim: RPN1 is an ER marker.

evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about cellular markers.

claim: The ERGIC fraction (F2) was most active in generating small vesicles active in LC3 lipidation.
source: We observed that the ERGIC fraction (F2) was most active in generating small vesicles active in LC3 lipidation, although it was less active in capturing cargo proteins into COPII vesicles than membranes in the P fraction (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The ERGIC fraction (F2) was less active in capturing cargo proteins into COPII vesicles than membranes in the P fraction.
source: We observed that the ERGIC fraction (F2) was most active in generating small vesicles active in LC3 lipidation, although it was less active in capturing cargo proteins into COPII vesicles than membranes in the P fraction (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The plasma membrane and endosome fraction (marked by transferrin receptor) was less potent in the generation of both COPII and lipidation-active vesicles.
source: The plasma membrane and endosome fraction (marked by transferrin receptor), and the Golgi fraction (marked by GM130) were less potent in the generation of both COPII and lipidation-active vesicles (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The Golgi fraction (marked by GM130) was less potent in the generation of both COPII and lipidation-active vesicles.
source: The plasma membrane and endosome fraction (marked by transferrin receptor), and the Golgi fraction (marked by GM130) were less potent in the generation of both COPII and lipidation-active vesicles (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Transferrin receptor is a marker for plasma membrane and endosome fraction.
source: The plasma membrane and endosome fraction (marked by transferrin receptor), and the Golgi fraction (marked by GM130) were less potent in the generation of both COPII and lipidation-active vesicles (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about cellular markers.

claim: GM130 is a marker for the Golgi fraction.
source: The plasma membrane and endosome fraction (marked by transferrin receptor), and the Golgi fraction (marked by GM130) were less potent in the generation of both COPII and lipidation-active vesicles (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about cellular markers.

claim: Depletion of the ERGIC membrane decreased the generation of small vesicles marked by COPII cargos (ERGIC53 and Sec22B) and active in LC3 lipidation.
source: Depletion of the ERGIC membrane decreased the generation of small vesicles marked by COPII cargos (ERGIC53 and Sec22B) and active in LC3 lipidation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), consistent with a role for the ERGIC as the donor membrane in generating lipidation-active vesicles.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The ERGIC is the donor membrane in generating lipidation-active vesicles.
source: Depletion of the ERGIC membrane decreased the generation of small vesicles marked by COPII cargos (ERGIC53 and Sec22B) and active in LC3 lipidation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), consistent with a role for the ERGIC as the donor membrane in generating lipidation-active vesicles.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the immunodepletion experiment.

claim: SAR1 (H79G) inhibited COPII budding and the generation of lipidation-active vesicles.
source: SAR1 (H79G) inhibited COPII budding and the generation of lipidation-active vesicles whereas BFA showed a marginal effect (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Brefeldin A (BFA) showed a marginal effect on COPII budding and the generation of lipidation-active vesicles.
source: SAR1 (H79G) inhibited COPII budding and the generation of lipidation-active vesicles whereas BFA showed a marginal effect (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: SAR1 (H79G) is a COPII inhibitor.
source: To test if COPII and COPI are involved in the generation of lipidation active vesicles, we used a COPII inhibitor SAR1 (H79G) and a COPI inhibitor brefeldin A (BFA) (Peyroche et al., 1999; Ward et al., 2001) in the cell-free small vesicle formation assay (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Brefeldin A (BFA) is a COPI inhibitor.
source: To test if COPII and COPI are involved in the generation of lipidation active vesicles, we used a COPII inhibitor SAR1 (H79G) and a COPI inhibitor brefeldin A (BFA) (Peyroche et al., 1999; Ward et al., 2001) in the cell-free small vesicle formation assay (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Cytosol collected from Sec23A-silenced Atg5 KO MEFs was less active in the generation of small vesicles competent as a template for lipidation of LC3.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 5A.

claim: Inhibition of COPII decreased LC3 lipidation in the 25K fraction but did not affect LC3 lipidation on the 100K fraction.
source: Inhibition of COPII decreased LC3 lipidation in the 25K fraction but did not affect LC3 lipidation on the 100K fraction (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: COPII acts on the ERGIC membrane to generate the lipidation-active membranes.
source: This result is consistent with the view that COPII acts on the ERGIC membrane to generate the lipidation-active membranes, i.e. the small vesicles are downstream products of COPII budding.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the differential effect of COPII inhibition on different membrane fractions.

claim: The small vesicles are downstream products of COPII budding.
source: This result is consistent with the view that COPII acts on the ERGIC membrane to generate the lipidation-active membranes, i.e. the small vesicles are downstream products of COPII budding.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the experimental data.

claim: Small vesicles decorated with endogenous LC3 (both LC3-I and -II) were generated in a PI3K-COPII-dependent manner in WT MEFs.
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6, small vesicles decorated with endogenous LC3 (both LC3-I and -II) were generated in a PI3K-COPII-dependent manner, whereas the packaging of COPII cargoes (SEC22B and ERGIC53) into small vesicles was COPII-dependent but PI3K-independent.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: The packaging of COPII cargoes (SEC22B and ERGIC53) into small vesicles was COPII-dependent but PI3K-independent.
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6, small vesicles decorated with endogenous LC3 (both LC3-I and -II) were generated in a PI3K-COPII-dependent manner, whereas the packaging of COPII cargoes (SEC22B and ERGIC53) into small vesicles was COPII-dependent but PI3K-independent.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: Small vesicles positive for the autophagic membrane protein ATG9 were generated independent of PI3K or COPII.
source: Noticeably, small vesicles positive for the autophagic membrane protein ATG9 were also generated in the reaction, but in this case vesicles formed independent of PI3K or COPII (Figure 2—figure supplement 6), suggesting that this potential source of autophagosomal membrane was generated in a process distinct from that of the LC3 lipidation active vesicles.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: ATG9 vesicles are generated in a process distinct from that of the LC3 lipidation active vesicles.
source: Noticeably, small vesicles positive for the autophagic membrane protein ATG9 were also generated in the reaction, but in this case vesicles formed independent of PI3K or COPII (Figure 2—figure supplement 6), suggesting that this potential source of autophagosomal membrane was generated in a process distinct from that of the LC3 lipidation active vesicles.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the differential requirements for ATG9 vesicle formation.

claim: ATG9 vesicles may come from the trans-Golgi network (TGN).
source: It is possible that the ATG9 vesicles come from the trans-Golgi network (TGN) as they have been shown to exit the TGN after starvation (Young et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ATG9 vesicles have been shown to exit the TGN after starvation.
source: It is possible that the ATG9 vesicles come from the trans-Golgi network (TGN) as they have been shown to exit the TGN after starvation (Young et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Depletion of SEC23A reduced the biogenesis of autophagosomes as revealed by the formation of starvation-induced lipidated LC3.

claim: Depletion of SEC23A reduced the appearance of LC3 puncta in WT MEFs and Hela cells.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7C-F.

claim: COPII is required for autophagosome biogenesis.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in the manuscript and citations to prior work.

claim: Under nutrient-rich conditions, a few LC3 puncta formed which did not overlap with COPII vesicles.
source: Under nutrient-rich conditions, a few LC3 puncta formed which did not overlap with COPII vesicles (Figure 2—figure supplement 8).

claim: Starvation induced a dramatic increase in LC3 puncta.
source: As expected, starvation induced a dramatic increase in LC3 puncta.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 8.

claim: On starvation, many small LC3 puncta colocalized with SEC31A whereas larger puncta did not.
